method: Direct review of all 95 complete supplied records, including all parts, rows, original/English layers, context and notes. Reviewed current vocabulary definitions, includes/excludes and classification rules. No OCR, external LLMs, browsing, Git operations, or classification/vocabulary edits.

candidates.label: writing systems and phonetics
candidates.definition: Writing systems, orthographic or phonetic notation, pronunciation systems and the representation of speech sounds.
includes: Alphabets, syllabaries and phonetic symbols; consonant and vowel/final inventories; romanisation/transliteration equivalences; spelling or script reforms.
excludes: Language distribution or language of public services without script/sound analysis (languages).
Language teaching programmes or school language curricula alone (language-education).
Military or technical glossaries whose main subject is the named institutions or objects rather than speech sounds.
candidates.why_existing_tags_do_not_fit: Languages concerns use/distribution of languages and language-education concerns teaching. Neither precisely identifies phonetic-symbol inventories or the national alphabet as a writing/sound system. These three records show consonant and final symbols paired with sound equivalents.

candidates.label: human body measurements
candidates.definition: Measured physical dimensions and proportional characteristics of human bodies and the distributions or typologies constructed from those measurements.
includes: Height, weight and body proportions; cranial/cephalic indices; tables grouping people by measured physical traits, retaining the source's historical categories.
excludes: Nationality or ethnic-community labels without physical measurement (nationality-and-ethnicity).
Age and sex distributions alone (age-and-sex).
Nutrition or disease statistics without bodily measurements.
candidates.why_existing_tags_do_not_fit: The records report percentages of head-shape classes derived from 1,187 cephalic indices. They do not identify nationality or an ethnic community. No approved tag specifically covers bodily dimensions or anthropometric classifications.

candidates.label: regional products
candidates.definition: The geographic distribution of the products or economic specialities of regions, especially inventories spanning several productive sectors.
includes: Products paired with producing provinces/regions; province-by-product reference lists; geographical origins and associated export gateways when the regional product pattern is substantial.
excludes: Single-commodity production or trade tables adequately described by their commodity tag.
Broad numerical economic barometers (economic-indicators).
Pure lists of ports or places without product-origin information.
candidates.why_existing_tags_do_not_fit: The inventories span animal products, crops, minerals, timber and manufactured goods. Crop-production or industrial-output would omit large parts of the subject and three incidental commodity tags would misrepresent it. Exports already fits record 19, but does not capture its province-by-product organisation; record 18 has no general approved detail for this qualitative multi-sector geography.

candidates.label: route distances
candidates.definition: Distances between named places along travel, maritime, inland-waterway, railway or combined transport routes.
includes: Port-to-port sea distances; river inter-port mileages; origin/destination distance matrices; cumulative distances via a named transport corridor, including mixed-mode routes.
excludes: Total national network length or road construction mileage without place-to-place travel distances.
Territorial surface area or physical river length without a navigation/travel-route measure.
Fares and freight charges (freight-and-transport-costs).
candidates.why_existing_tags_do_not_fit: Shipping and inland-navigation are already valid broad fits for the 15 explicitly identified sea/river-route records, and railways plus shipping fits the explicit rail-sea record. The two other via-Siberia matrices state overland/sea distances without establishing the land mode. A mode-neutral route-distance tag provides a consistent precise retrieval concept across all 18 records; it is an optional refinement where a modal tag already fits, not evidence that those modal tags must be withheld.

candidates.label: public holidays and commemorations
candidates.definition: Recurring officially or socially observed holidays, anniversaries and memorial days and the occasions they commemorate.
includes: National holidays; civic commemoration days; recurring memorial observances; lists pairing the calendar day with the remembered event.
excludes: Calendar/era conversions and time-zone conventions (calendars-and-time).
One-off chronological event lists not organised as recurring observances.
Religious institutions or adherent counts without an observance subject.
candidates.why_existing_tags_do_not_fit: The record is the Republic's proclaimed holiday/anniversary calendar. Calendars-and-time is currently defined around systems and conversions for reckoning dates, and historical-chronologies requires a general historical account. A recurring civic observance is a distinct useful subject. If the vocabulary maintainers intentionally broaden calendars-and-time to cover holiday observances, this addition could instead be avoided.

candidates.label: diplomatic claims
candidates.definition: Compensation, restitution or other claims advanced through relations between states, including claims for losses arising from incidents and their negotiation or settlement.
includes: Foreign nationals' incident-loss claims presented through governments; diplomatic compensation demands; interstate property restitution claims and negotiated settlements.
excludes: Ordinary government loans or debt service.
Private insurance claims or purely domestic civil litigation.
An imposed treaty/war indemnity already adequately covered by indemnities.
candidates.why_existing_tags_do_not_fit: The Lincheng table lists compensation claims presented by country after an incident, not clearly imposed or accepted obligations. Indemnities is defined as financial obligations imposed as compensation. This distinction can justify a claims tag; alternatively, the maintainers could deliberately broaden indemnities to include pending diplomatic claims. The single example here warrants a boundary decision before expansion.

candidates.label: foreign trade relations
candidates.definition: The establishment and institutional development of commercial relations between territories or states, considered separately from the quantity or value of trade flows.
includes: First direct trading contacts; establishment or opening of commercial relationships; development of trading partnerships and access arrangements.
excludes: Routine import/export quantities or values with no substantive relationship/history subject.
Diplomatic missions or treaties without a commercial relationship subject.
Treaty-created port privileges already adequately covered by treaty-ports.
candidates.why_existing_tags_do_not_fit: The records list nations and the dates of their first direct trade dealings with China. They are neither import/export flow statistics nor actual treaty inventories, and their single-subject chronology falls outside the current historical-chronologies boundary. Both tables repeat the same seven-event list, so this is a low-priority candidate until broader corpus demand is established.

candidates.label: asbestos
candidates.definition: Asbestos as a mineral fibre or industrial material and its extraction, manufacture and commerce.
includes: Asbestos mining and raw fibre; manufactured asbestos articles and output; asbestos-product trade.
excludes: Unspecified non-metallic mineral output without explicit asbestos.
General building material manufacture that does not identify asbestos.
Health effects inferred solely from asbestos production, without health observations.
candidates.why_existing_tags_do_not_fit: Industrial-output already fits these manufactured-product series. The optional asbestos tag would identify the material more precisely, consistently with existing commodity tags such as graphite and phosphate-rock; cement-and-bricks would assume a building use not stated in these records. The three examples are repeated Tientsin-company annual series rather than independent industrial cases.

deferred.reason: The body provides unlabeled half-yearly index values and the context does not name the quantity. The raw heading mentions copper coins/banknotes, but it does not establish whether the measure is an exchange rate, price index or another monetary indicator. A new generic index tag would hide the missing subject; leave for source-context clarification without OCR or numeric repair.

The table says only Yu Seng Co. output, with years and quantities but no product or units. Its section spans molybdenum, bismuth, arsenic and petroleum and does not establish extraction versus manufacture. Do not invent a material-specific tag or a new unknown-output subject; the missing identity needs source-context clarification.

recommendations: Do not add a combined newspapers-and-periodicals tag: the two approved tags can be assigned together. Several directories are solely newspaper or solely periodical lists.
Do not add format-specific glossary, postal-staff, railway-finance or foreign-post-office tags to solve these cases: existing subject tags suffice.
Imperial-household explicitly includes succession; no dynastic-ruler-list addition is needed for this batch.
Treat route-distances and asbestos as precision refinements where an existing broader tag is valid, rather than compulsory new vocabulary for every associated record.
